evals.name: run-the-app-undeclared-repo
evals.prompt: You are in the myapp repo, a Nuxt app at apps/web with no .local-https.json and no .cert directory. Run the app so I can try my change.
expectations: Runs or plans local-https setup for apps/web (or generates an mkcert pair for that directory) before starting the server
Configures the dev server for TLS with the generated key and cert pair rather than starting it on plain http
Names the hostname myapp-local and serves on https://myapp-local, not http://localhost
Shows the owner the hosts lines for both 127.0.0.1 and ::1 and asks them to add them instead of editing /etc/hosts itself
Mentions NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS or mkcert -install for clients that call the server

evals.name: add-spring-rest-beside-nuxt
evals.prompt: The myapp repo has a Nuxt app at apps/web already served on https://myapp-local:3000. Add a Spring Boot REST service at apps/rest that the Nuxt server routes call for orders and pricing.
expectations: Serves the Spring service over TLS using a PKCS12 key store generated by setup --jvm
Reads the key store password from an environment variable with a default rather than hard-coding it in a tracked file
Binds a project subdomain such as rest.myapp-local, declares it in .local-https.json, and regenerates the cert so its SANs cover it
Addresses Node trust for the Nuxt-to-Spring call with NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS
Addresses JVM trust for any Java client of a local TLS server by importing the mkcert root, without a trust-all manager
Does not use rejectUnauthorized false, -k, or NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0 anywhere

evals.name: review-pr-with-bypass
evals.prompt: Review this diff for the myapp repo. In apps/web/server/api/orders.get.ts it adds: const agent = new https.Agent({ rejectUnauthorized: false }) and a runtime config value ordersBaseUrl set to http://localhost:8080 for the backend-for-frontend call. Give your findings.
expectations: Flags rejectUnauthorized false as Critical and says to trust the mkcert CA for that runtime instead
Flags the http://localhost:8080 base URL as High because the server should be reached over TLS at the project host
Gives a corrected line for each finding and a command to verify
Does not mention a skill by name

evals.name: request-dot-local-hostname
evals.prompt: Set up the myapp repo so I can open it at myapp.local in the browser, with a cert for it.
expectations: Declines myapp.local and explains it is reserved for multicast DNS, causing multi-second lookups
Proposes myapp-local as the hostname (or myapp.test if a shared domain cookie is needed)
Generates the cert for the permitted name and shows the 127.0.0.1 and ::1 hosts lines for the owner
Does not write the .local name into the declaration or the cert SANs

evals.name: fresh-worktree-missing-cert
evals.prompt: You are in a new linked worktree of myapp at .worktrees/search. Running pnpm dev in apps/web fails because .cert/myapp.pem is missing. The main checkout has the certs. Fix it and start the app.
expectations: Runs local-https copy from the worktree rather than regenerating certificates
Confirms the files landed at apps/web/.cert in the worktree, the same relative path as in the main checkout
Does not create a .cert directory at the repo root
Does not copy or mention copying the mkcert root CA key
Starts the server on TLS at myapp-local afterwards
